name: Juming Museum
funding: Ju Ming Culture and Education Foundation (assets NT$167M, 2020), plus admissions, friends scheme and exhibition sponsors.
watch: No full funder list is published. A 2026 show credits the Ministry of Culture, an InterContinental hotel and a metalwork firm.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2016 to 2025 with CPA-audited statements, a donor thanks page and a named board of nine.

name: Künstlerhaus Bethanien
funding: Institutional funding comes from the Berlin Senate Department for Culture, cut by about EUR 149k in 2025; national arts councils and KfW Stiftung fund residencies.
watch: Residency house founded 1974. About 30 foreign arts councils and ministries pay for its studio places.
records_note: Bethanien names its partners and funders on one undated page but posts no annual reports, accounts or board; its team page names two directors.

name: Kamloops Art Gallery
funding: City of Kamloops, Province of BC, BC Arts Council, Canada Council, Thompson-Nicola Regional District, Audain and Hamber foundations. BC Lottery Corporation sponsors free Thursday admission.
watch: BCLC is a provincial Crown corporation. The Cullen Commission (2022) found it ignored police warnings about casino money laundering until 2015.
records_note: Posts its 2025 annual report and signed 2025 financial statements, names donors in tiers since January 2024, and lists its trustees in the report.

name: Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Kaohsiung City administrative corporation since 2017; 2025 donors: Applied Materials Taiwan, Rotary 3510, art foundations, shipping, King's Town Bank foundation.
watch: Named funders, all allowed: Applied Materials Taiwan, King's Town Bank's charity foundation and Fulong shipping. The only row was a 2024 sketching ban.
records_note: Annual records for 2016 to 2025 and yearly donation ledgers 2017 to 2025 are on its site; no accounts or board list found.

name: Kapelica Gallery (Kersnikova Institute)
funding: Small NGO venue (2025), funded by Slovenia's Ministry of Culture, the City of Ljubljana and EU programmes.
watch: Research-art gallery founded in 1995 by the Student Organisation of the University of Ljubljana (ŠOU). Run by Kersnikova with the BioTehna lab and the Rampa hacker space.
records_note: Kersnikova lists 21 supporters by name but posts no annual reports, accounts or board; its Crew page names a director and staff.

name: Kaskadenkondensator (Kasko)
funding: Swiss Arts Council Pro Helvetia, Canton of Basel-Stadt Cultural Department, non-profit patron association; artist-run space.
watch: Located in the historic Warteck brewery complex; artist-run project space for performance, process-based art, and feminist collaboration since 1994.

name: Kassák Múzeum
funding: Petőfi Literary Museum Public Directorate, National Cultural Fund of Hungary; public museum trust.
watch: Research museum on Lajos Kassák, avant-garde socialist internationalism and workers' movements.

name: Kathmandu Triennale
funding: Siddhartha Arts Foundation with Nepal Academy of Fine Arts (2026); 2022 edition backed by embassies, Saraf Foundation, Gorkha Brewery, Himalayan Bank, Toyota.
watch: The 2026 supporters page lists only organisers. The 2022 roster has no excluded names.
records_note: The current Triennale site lists only its two organisers as supporters, with patrons empty, and posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Kestner Gesellschaft
funding: Lower Saxony culture ministry, Region Hannover, NDR Kultur, foundations and 32 corporate partners including Talanx, Hannover Rück, GETEC Gruppe, NORD/LB, Bertelsmann, Deutsche Messe and VHV.
watch: Talanx drew an Insure Our Future campaign over oil and gas cover; none targets Kestner. Partner GETEC Gruppe now runs grids and renewables.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; it names 32 corporate partners undated and lists a ten-person board plus about 30 advisory board members.

name: Khalil Sakakini Cultural Center
watch: Independent non-profit in a historic 1927 Palestinian mansion; dedicated to visual arts, literature, and Palestinian identity.

name: Kharkiv Municipal Gallery
funding: Founded 1996 as Ukraine's first gallery with municipal status. The city council culture department decides on its premises.
watch: Upper halls closed since 2022 and its White Cube now serves the city's news studio. The ARTbasement, also a shelter, reopened in September 2023.
records_note: The gallery's site returned HTTP 403, so nothing could be checked; it is a city council institution.

name: Khoj International Artists' Association
funding: Artist-run since 1997. Top supporters: Prince Claus Fund, Goethe-Institut New Delhi and Ford Foundation; capital circle includes Apeejay Trust, Inlaks India Foundation, Weikfield; benefactor Sangeeta Jindal.
watch: Benefactor Sangeeta Jindal (JSW Foundation): JSW is mostly steel; its power arm is about 5% of group revenue (US$1.1B of US$23B).
records_note: No annual report or audited accounts, only foreign-contribution filings from 2012; it names donors by tier, undated, and lists an eight-member board plus advisors.
